title: Find your investors
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: If you had three months of money left, where would you look first?
I asked a student to go through the process in front of everyone. We need money, we will run out in six months. He can get desperate and look for money anywhere, but who are we looking for?

The student said: people who have invested in erosion-mitigation companies, the closest thing to it, then pitch them. I asked what words they would put into a search. He helped: private equity, green infrastructure, environmental infrastructure.
Do you want venture capital, private equity or angel investors? I said he would go for all of them. A student added family offices.
I like to read a lot of press releases, I said. Add PR to the search words and see whether a managing partner is saying: we're actively looking to invest in this space.

First look at what the industry is doing, I said. Is it fragmented, with a lot of little companies and no big one rolling them up? What is the biggest company and its revenue? Are the big-money players getting good returns? Align with the ones looking at swallowing up companies in the sector.
A student said: category makers are a popular trend. Venture firms look for a company that is one of one, a new segment of a sector.

A student suggested conventions: shaking hands with people who share your ideas, and finding two or three who are really interested among thousands. You can tell the vibe of the person when you meet them.

I agreed, and told how a young colleague printed cards with no company and went to a landscaping convention. He met a man who gave him fifty thousand dollars to open an office. I met a company he later merged with at a convention too.

It's intimidating, I said: eighteen hundred companies on a floor. Do the research before you go, see who is going to be there, have a specific goal, and write to people ahead: I'd love to have a cup of coffee, or invite you to dinner.
What are the keywords you would search tonight?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the keywords you would search for investors in your sector.
Write the types you would try: venture, private equity, angel, family office.
Write what the press says the big investors are looking for.
Write a convention you could go to and who you want to meet.
Write the email you would send before you go.

check.q: What did I add to his search to find press releases?
What did a student suggest as a place to find investors?
What did I say to do before a convention?
choices: Research who will be there and have a specific goal

recap: Search the sector, read the press, go where they are. Have a goal.
